subject_definitions
<Subject 1> is the adult East Asian woman from <Picture 1>, preserving her brunette updo, crystal hair ornament, earrings and pale-blue embellished evening gown.
<Subject 2> is the adult woman from <Picture 2>, preserving her blue-and-white hair, blue glasses, heart necklace, blue crop top, knitted cardigan, pleated skirt and white platform heels.
<Subject 3> is the adult woman from <Picture 3>, preserving her blonde bob, earrings, embroidered navy silk qipao and black heels.
At the opening of <Video 1>, the screen-left mannequin corresponds permanently to <Subject 1>, the foreground-right mannequin with her back toward the camera corresponds permanently to <Subject 2>, and the remaining mannequin corresponds permanently to <Subject 3>.
<Video 1> provides the seating arrangement, conversational gestures, action timing, spatial relationships and complete camera path. The camera must visibly travel through the group rather than remaining outside the characters.
summary
reference generation + video editing. Replace the three white mannequins in <Video 1> with <Subject 1>, <Subject 2> and <Subject 3>. They sit around a small table in an elegant afternoon café, chatting naturally. The camera enters the group, passes between the seated women, glides through their shared conversational space, passes close to shoulders and hands, and exits through the opposite side before pulling back. All viewpoint changes are caused by camera animation, not by the characters rotating.
retention_analysis
<Subject 1>, <Subject 2> and <Subject 3>: fully_preserved — preserve their individual identities, hairstyles, clothing, accessories and stable assignment.
<Video 1>: partially_preserved — preserve character positions, gestures, conversational timing, framing progression and camera movement, while replacing the mannequins and environment.
Camera path: attribute_transfer — reproduce the source framing changes as a pronounced forward-moving camera that threads through the group, passes between the characters and exits from the opposite side.
detailed_description
The target video is a photorealistic cinematic lifestyle scene in an elegant café during a warm, peaceful afternoon. Tall arched windows, cream walls, oak furniture, linen curtains, indoor plants and soft floral arrangements surround the group. Golden sunlight produces natural highlights, soft shadows and gentle atmospheric depth.
[Shot 1] The three women sit on upholstered chairs around a small round marble table. Their chairs, hips and feet remain fixed in world space. They only perform conversational hand gestures, blinking, subtle head turns, eye contact, nodding and natural mouth movement. They must not rotate their chairs or turn their entire bodies to generate new viewing angles.
The shot begins as a wide over-the-shoulder composition from behind <Subject 2>. The camera immediately performs a slow, deliberate dolly forward and visibly enters the group. It passes through the open gap between <Subject 2>’s shoulder and <Subject 3>, crossing from outside the seating arrangement into the inner conversational space.
The camera continues moving through the group rather than orbiting from a distant radius. It glides close to the edge of the marble table, with cups, pastries and flowers briefly passing through the lower foreground. It threads between the characters without touching them, creating strong spatial parallax between foreground shoulders, moving hands, chair backs, tableware and the café background.
As the camera passes through the center of the group, <Subject 2>’s shoulder and blue-white hair briefly create a natural foreground wipe. The lens then passes beside <Subject 3>’s gesturing hand and moves toward <Subject 1>, transitioning smoothly into a close-up. The close-up is produced by the camera physically approaching her; <Subject 1> does not lean toward the lens.
The camera continues past <Subject 1>’s near shoulder, revealing her profile through the curved camera path. It then travels out of the group through the opposite gap between <Subject 1> and <Subject 3>. After clearly exiting the seated group, the camera makes a smooth pullback and a gentle lateral arc, progressively revealing all three women again and ending in a balanced wide composition from a new side.
The motion must feel like a stabilized gimbal camera weaving through a small crowd: continuous forward travel, close foreground occlusions, pronounced parallax and a clear entrance into and exit from the group. Do not simulate the effect by rotating the characters or spinning the background.
Maintain safe physical clearance throughout the camera path. The virtual lens must never clip through faces, torsos, hair, hands, chairs, clothing, cups or the table. Preserve stable character identity and assignment. Avoid identity swapping, duplicated people, disappearing glasses, changing clothes, malformed hands, intersecting arms, floating tableware, foot sliding, unstable backgrounds or sudden camera teleportation.
overall_soundscape
Quiet afternoon café ambience with porcelain clinks, subtle coffee-pouring sounds, fabric movement, indistinct conversational murmurs and faint birds outside. Foreground café sounds become slightly clearer as the camera passes through the group.
non_diegetic_music
Soft afternoon jazz with gentle piano, brushed drums and warm upright bass, maintaining a relaxed tempo beneath the café ambience.
